label: Instance Registry
info:
SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the dbus service name and VRM/device instance of every virtual device the Node-RED flows publish to Venus OS.

Why: the victron palette derives the service name from the Node-RED node ID (com.victronenergy.<class>.virtual_<nodeId>) and lets localsettings auto-assign the instance in registration order. Any regenerated node ID or reset settings entry mints a brand-new service + instance, and Signal K keys its paths off both -> orphan paths accumulate (tanks.freshWater.81/83/85/89 etc.).

Fix: the 'Instance Registry (single source of truth)' function node holds the ONLY table mapping each device to a hand-assigned instance in the reserved block 200-255 (Venus auto-assigns native devices from 0 upward, so no collision is possible). On startup and on manual inject the flow idempotently pre-seeds /Settings/Devices/virtual_<id>/ClassAndVrmInstance (AddSetting keeps an existing value), pins it with SetValue when it differs, then audits the LIVE services. Existing services are updated in place - the service name never changes, so a redeploy can never create a second copy.

Enforcement runs as ONE python3 batch over a single dbus connection (heredoc via the exec node). The per-device dbus CLI approach was abandoned: each CLI call spawns a Python interpreter (~1.5s at load avg ~4), so the full device list blew past the exec timeout and the run was truncated mid-pass.

Statuses: OK (pinned and live-correct), PINNED (settings corrected this pass), RECONVERGE (settings pinned but the running service registered before the pin landed - one more deploy converges it), NOT-RUNNING (registry row whose flow is not deployed), ERROR (dbus call failed), orphan (settings entry for a dead service - removable via the manual cleanup inject), unmanaged (LIVE service missing from the registry - add a row; never removed automatically).

Rules: this table is the only authority for instances. Never derive an instance from array index, discovery order, loop counter, timestamp or hash. Never reuse a number, even after deleting a device. Keep node IDs hand-written, dot-free and never regenerated. Allocation is mirrored in specification.md; verify with verify_pinning.py (3x Node-RED restart, no new instances allowed).
